title: Uber begins self-driving robotaxi trial in Manchester
key_facts: Uber has begun a trial of self-driving cars on the streets of Manchester, UK.
The cars use technology from partners Pony (Pony.ai) and Verne, with whom Uber launched Europe's first autonomous taxi service in Zagreb, Croatia.
The tests involve mapping the streets with a safety driver behind the wheel and no passengers.
Limited passenger services started last month in London with a safety driver, using Wayve cars.
There has been no official application to launch passenger services in Manchester.
Opposition from Uber drivers, unions and London politicians is mounting; GMB and ADCU say thousands of jobs will be lost.
Uber expects robotaxi trips in as many as 15 cities worldwide by the end of 2026.
quote_evidence: Uber has begun a trial of autonomous vehicles on the streets of Manchester as it looks to bring robotaxis to cities around the UK.
The tests involve the company mapping the streets of the city in north-west England with a safety driver behind the wheel and no passengers.
There has been no official application to launch passenger services in Manchester so far.
why_it_matters_hint: Robotaxi testing reaches a second UK city, but without passengers, without a licence application and with driver unions opposed.
